title: Aquarium Heater Duty-Cycle Spike
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=aquarium:sensor
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(heater_on_pct) as heater_pct, avg(temp_c) as temp by tank _time
| where heater_pct>60 AND temp<24
| sort - heater_pct
description: Measures how hard the aquarium heater is working and catches tanks that are spending lots of time heating without actually holding temperature.
value: A struggling heater is often the first sign of equipment failure or heat loss, and aquatic life pays the price long before humans notice.
implementation: Forward tank temperature and heater-state metrics; review daily when duty cycle spikes without stable temperature.
visualization: Daily chart of heater duty cycle versus tank temperature.
grandmaExplanation: It checks when the aquarium heater is working very hard but the tank still is not staying warm enough.
